route.name: Cairo-Aswan Railway (Upper Egypt Main Line)
route.description: Upper Egypt Nile-valley trunk; luxury 'Sunshine Express'
route.notes: ADDED as a 12th route from the Railway Wonders article + Wikipedia station list. Not in the original project 11; confirm you want it in the canonical set.  [established] Built in stages: Cairo–Assiut by 1874 (230 mi); Assiut–Luxor by 1898 (340 mi, Nile crossing at Nag Hammadi); Kena–Aswan by the private Kena-Aswan Railway Company; Aswan–Shellal was an 1884 military line, absorbed 1898. route.history: The Upper Egypt Nile-valley main line, built southward in stages: Cairo–Assiut by 1874, Assiut–Luxor by 1898 (crossing the Nile at Nag Hammadi). The Kena–Aswan section was built by the private Kena-Aswan Railway Company; the Aswan–Shellal section began as an 1884 military line for the first Sudan campaign and was regauged to standard gauge in 1926. By the mid-1930s three trains a day ran each way Cairo–Luxor (~12 hours) and two a day to Aswan/Shellal (480 miles, ~17 hours).
